articles.title: Catherine talks about mortality and cancer in new documentary clip
articles.summary: The Princess of Wales talks about her cancer journey in a new clip from the upcoming BBC documentary, Heal.
articles.body:
The Princess of Wales has said cancer made her confront her own vulnerabilities, in a new clip from her upcoming documentary, Heal.

"When you're faced with your own mortality, you have to accept that life is not infinite," Catherine says.

In March 2024, Catherine revealed that she had a cancer diagnosis and was receiving chemotherapy.

In a previously released trailer for the documentary, Catherine is seen hugging her children and her husband, the Prince of Wales, as she completed the Three Peaks Challenge earlier this year.

Heal will air on BBC One on Sunday, 29 November.

articles.standfirst: Motorista do caminhão ficou preso às ferragens e precisou ser resgatado pelo Corpo de Bombeiros. Acidente aconteceu na tarde desta segunda-feira (23), no bairro Jorge Teixeira
articles.summary: Acidente de caminhão em Manaus: veículo perdeu o controle em ladeira do Jorge Teixeira, atingiu uma casa e exigiu resgate complexo de motorista preso às ferragens.
articles.body:
Um caminhão de pequeno porte que transportava materiais de construção perdeu o controle ao descer de uma ladeira e bateu contra uma casa na rua Peixe-Cachorro, bairro Jorge Teixeira, Zona Leste de Manaus . O acidente aconteceu por volta de 15h desta segunda-feira (23). Assista acima .

De acordo com o Corpo de Bombeiros, o motorista ficou com as duas pernas presas na parte inferior do veículo e precisou ser socorrido. Militares do 3º Grupamento de Bombeiros Militar utilizaram equipamentos hidráulicos para afastar o painel do veículo e libertar a vítima.

Após o resgate, o motorista foi entregue à equipe do Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu), que realizou o atendimento pré-hospitalar e encaminhou o homem a uma unidade de saúde.

Não foram divulgadas informações sobre o estado de saúde da vítima.

Caminhão de pequeno porte se chocou contra casa no bairro Jorge Teixeira, na Zona Leste de Manaus. — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

articles.summary: A Universidade Federal Rural da Amazônia abre inscrições para 57 vagas de professor com remuneração de até R$ 13,7 mil e auxílio-alimentação em seis cidades do Pará.
articles.body:
Universidade Federal Rural da Amazônia (Ufra). — Foto: Divulgação

A Universidade Federal Rural da Amazônia ( Ufra ) lançou edital de concurso público com 57 vagas efetivas para professores. As inscrições começam em 4 de dezembro e seguem até o dia 18 do mesmo mês, em 2026.

A remuneração total bruta pode chegar a R$ 13.753,96 , conforme a titulação do candidato.

A taxa de inscrição é de R$ 180, com possibilidade de isenção para candidatos que atendam aos critérios do edital.As provas estão previstas para fevereiro de 2027.

As oportunidades estão distribuídas pelos seis campi da universidade:

Há vagas em Medicina Veterinária, Matemática, Ciências Biológicas, Engenharias, Administração, Letras e Enfermagem, entre outras áreas.

A formação exigida depende da vaga e pode incluir graduação específica e título de mestre ou doutor.

Os valores variam conforme a titulação apresentada pelo candidato:

Os valores incluem vencimento básico e retribuição por titulação. Além disso, o edital prevê auxílio-alimentação de R$ 1.192 e outros benefícios previstos na legislação.

As inscrições devem ser feitas exclusivamente pela internet, de 4 a 18 de dezembro, no Sistema Integrado de Gestão de Recursos Humanos (SIGRH) , na opção destinada aos concursos.

A taxa é de R$ 180. No momento da inscrição, o candidato deverá apresentar:

Documento oficial de identificação com foto;

Currículo Lattes acompanhado dos documentos comprobatórios, conforme as orientações do edital.

Inscritos no Cadastro Único (CadÚnico) com renda familiar mensal por pessoa de até meio salário mínimo;

O pedido deve ser feito entre 4 e 7 de dezembro, durante o preenchimento do formulário de inscrição. É necessário enviar a documentação comprobatória exigida no edital.

A divulgação dos pedidos aceitos e negados está prevista para 9 de dezembro. O prazo para apresentar recurso será nos dias 9 e 10 do mesmo mês.

Das 57 vagas, 20 são destinadas às políticas de ações afirmativas. Confira a distribuição:

Os candidatos às vagas reservadas deverão seguir os procedimentos de confirmação das autodeclarações e de verificação documental. As regras e os prazos estão no edital.

O concurso será composto por três etapas: Prova escrita de conhecimentos específicos; Prova didática; Avaliação de títulos.

As provas estão previstas para ocorrer de 15 a 26 de fevereiro de 2027. O resultado final deve ser divulgado em 23 de março de 2027, com homologação no dia seguinte.

articles.title: Três casos de Mpox são confirmados no sudoeste da Bahia | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítimas são dois homens e uma mulher. Registros aconteceram nas cidade de Vitória da Conquista e Paramirim.
articles.summary: Vítimas são dois homens e uma mulher. Registros aconteceram nas cidade de Vitória da Conquista e Paramirim
articles.body:
Três casos de Mpox foram confirmados no sudoeste da Bahia nos últimos dias. Um deles aconteceu na cidade de Vitória da Conquista e os outros dois em Paramirim . Todos os pacientes são monitorados pela Vigilância Epidemiológica.

A pessoa de Vitória da Conquista é um homem, que não teve a idade detalhada. Conforme apurou a TV Sudoeste, afiliada da Rede Bahia na região, ele começou a apresentar os sintomas no fim de outubro, porém a confirmação só saiu no domingo (22). É o primeiro caso do ano no município.

Atualmente, segundo a prefeitura, o homem passa bem e segue em isolamento domiciliar, com acompanhamento da equipe de saúde. Além dele, pessoas que tiveram contato próximo também são monitorados.

Um outro caso, de um adulto que apresentou sintomas suspeitos, é investigado na cidade. Enquanto isso, ele também está em isolamento e em monitoramento. Não há detalhes sobre o estado de saúde do homem.

Já os casos de Paramirim foram confirmados pela prefeitura nesta segunda-feira (23). As duas pessoas são um pai e sua filha, que apresentam boa evolução clínica e seguem acompanhados.

A gestão municipal informou que os casos são isolados e estão relacionados ao contato com pessoas de Salvador que estão infectadas.

Segundo levantamento do Ministério da Saúde, 12 casos foram confirmados no estado, somente em 2026.

A Mpox é uma doença infecciosa causada por um vírus, que pode provocar lesões na pele iniciadas como manchas, e que podem evoluir para bolhas e feridas. Outros sintomas incluem febre, dor de cabeça e dores musculares.

Ao apresentar algum desses sintomas, a orientação é procurar uma unidade de saúde, utilizando máscara cirúrgica. É importante também evitar contato físico próximo com outras pessoas.

A transmissão acontece principalmente pelo contato próximo e prolongado com uma pessoa infectada. Existe vacina oferecida pelo Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS), mas conforme a orientação da Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS), o imunizante atende a públicos determinados.

Conforme especialista, geralmente portadores do HIV, sendo avaliados pelo médico, ou pessoas que fazem uso da profilaxia pré-exposição (PrEP).

articles.title: Bombeiros fazem buscas por mulher que caiu no rio Tamanduateí durante temporal na Zona Sul de SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Ocorrência foi registrada na noite de domingo (22), quando o rio transbordou; testemunhas disseram que mulher usava vestido roxo. Trabalhos foram retomados nesta segunda e devem continuar na terça-feira (24).
articles.summary: Ocorrência foi registrada na noite de domingo (22), quando o rio transbordou; testemunhas disseram que mulher usava vestido roxo. Trabalhos foram retomados nesta segunda e devem continuar na terça-feira (24).
articles.body:
O Corpo de Bombeiros retomou nesta segunda-feira (23) as buscas por uma mulher que caiu no rio Tamanduateí, na Vila Monumento, na Zona Sul de São Paulo. A suspeita é que ela tenha sido arrastada pela correnteza durante as fortes chuvas de domingo (22), quando o rio transbordou.

A ocorrência foi registrada por volta das 19h, mas, como as buscas só podem ser realizadas durante o dia, os trabalhos começaram na manhã desta segunda e devem continuar na terça-feira (24), segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros.

Segundo a corporação, a possível queda ocorreu nas proximidades da Praça Lyon, na Avenida Teresa Cristina.

De acordo com informações repassadas por testemunhas aos bombeiros, a mulher estaria usando um vestido roxo.

Até a última atualização desta reportagem, ela ainda não havia sido oficialmente dada como desaparecida por familiares ou amigos.

Todas as regiões da cidade de São Paulo entraram em estado de atenção para alagamentos no domingo (22), segundo o Centro de Gerenciamento de Emergências Climáticas (CGE), da Prefeitura.

O alto volume de chuva deixou moradores ilhados na Estrada do M’Boi Mirim, na altura do Jardim Capela, Zona Sul da capital. Em São Bernardo do Campo, a chuva afetou a infraestrutura de um shopping e fez parte do teto da praça de alimentação ceder. Uma "cachoeira" se formou no local.

Rio Tamanduateí, na região da Avenida do Estado, Centro de São Paulo. — Foto: Divulgação/GESP

Nesta segunda (23), todas as regiões da cidade de São Paulo voltaram a entrar em estado de atenção para alagamentos , segundo o Centro de Gerenciamento de Emergências Climáticas (CGE).

Segundo o órgão, áreas de instabilidade vindas do interior devem atuar na capital paulista de forma isolada, mas com tendência a se espalhar.

Um alagamento na Avenida Miguel Inácio Curi, na Zona Leste, deixou carros submersos. A TV Globo registrou um veículo quase todo coberto pela água na da Rua Guirá-Acangatara, próximo à Avenida Aricanduva (vídeo acima).

A Companhia de Engenharia de Tráfego informou que o Túnel Anhangabaú está bloqueado preventivamente no sentido Aeroporto desde as 16h36. Às 17h13, a pista central do sentido Santana também foi bloqueada.

À TV Globo, a porta-voz do Corpo de Bombeiros, tenente Olívia Perrone Cazo, alertou para os riscos de acidentes durante episódios de enchentes e pediu que a população evite se colocar em situações de perigo.

"Infelizmente, a gente tem essa realidade aqui no município, que realmente tem muitas enchentes e a força da água é muito grande. Às vezes, a pessoa fica realmente encurralada. É difícil de escapar", afirmou.

A tenente também reforçou que nenhum bem material deve ser colocado acima da segurança das pessoas.

"Cuide de você, da sua família, não se arrisque de forma alguma. Não deixe um bem patrimonial valer mais que sua vida", disse.

articles.standfirst: Forte chuva atingiu diferentes bairros e distritos da cidade.
articles.summary: Forte chuva atingiu diferentes bairros e distritos da cidade.
articles.body:
Temporal provoca alagamentos e queda de árvores em Barra do Piraí — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Barra do Piraí

A Prefeitura de Barra do Piraí mobilizou equipes da Defesa Civil e de diferentes secretarias municipais para atender às ocorrências provocadas pela forte chuva que atingiu a cidade na noite desta segunda-feira (23). Foram registrados alagamentos, quedas de árvores e interrupções no fornecimento de energia elétrica em diferentes pontos do município.

As ocorrências foram registradas no bairros Vila Helena, Vale do Ipiranga, Oficina Velha, Represa, Centro, Química, nos distritos de Vargem Alegre e Dorândia, além da RJ-137, estrada que liga Barra do Piraí ao distrito de Ipiabas.

Segundo a Defesa Civil, o volume de chuva em um curto intervalo de tempo sobrecarregou o sistema de drenagem em alguns pontos. As equipes já estavam de prontidão por causa do alerta meteorológico e seguem monitorando os índices de chuva e as áreas consideradas de maior risco, em conjunto com o Corpo de Bombeiros e as secretarias de Serviços Públicos e Assistência Social.

O maior acumulado foi registrado no Vale do Ipiranga, com 72 milímetros de chuva. No Centro, na Rua Novo México, foram 42,4 mm. Também houve registro de 26,2 mm na Metalúrgica, 25 mm em Dorândia, 14,4 mm na Roseira e 12,2 mm no Areal. Os dados foram atualizados às 19h40 pela prefeitura.

Segundo a prefeitura, de acordo com a previsão meteorológica, há possibilidade de novos volumes expressivos de chuva nos próximos dias. A expectativa é de 20,5 mm na quarta-feira (25) e 25,4 mm na quinta-feira (26). Para o fim de semana, são previstos 27,7 mm no domingo (29) e 22,1 mm na segunda-feira (30).

A Defesa Civil orienta os moradores a acompanharem os alertas oficiais, evitarem deslocamentos desnecessários durante períodos de chuva intensa e não atravessarem áreas alagadas, a pé ou de carro. Em caso de sinais de risco, a recomendação é procurar um local seguro.

Em caso de emergência, a Defesa Civil pode ser acionada pelo telefone 199 e o Corpo de Bombeiros pelo 193.

articles.title: Ballymena riots: Tracy and Kelvin Kane jailed for 'disgraceful' acts
articles.summary: The judge said Kelvin and Tracy Kane were both "a total disgrace to the decent law-abiding citizens of Ballymena".
articles.body:
A mother and son described as ringleaders of rioting that targeted ethnic minorities have been jailed for what a judge called their "disgraceful activities".

Kelvin Kane, 32, of HMP Maghaberry, was jailed for four years on Monday after admitting 17 charges connected with rioting in Ballymena in the summer of 2025.

His mother Tracy Kane, 51, of Galgorm Street in the town, was jailed for two years after admitting two counts including encouraging and assisting her son's crimes.

Kelvin Kane's crimes included setting fire to a flat, which forced a family including a pregnant woman to be rescued.

Antrim Crown Court was told Kelvin Kane was both an instigator and organiser of the first night of violent disorder in Ballymena on 9 June 2025, which the judge called "an orgy of violence".

Kelvin Kane's offences included one count of riot, seven of criminal damage and one of arson being reckless as to whether life was endangered.

CCTV and police body-worn camera footage covering almost two hours was shown to the court at an earlier hearing on Thursday.

It showed Kelvin Kane helping to build a barricade on the junction of Clonavon Road and Clonavon Terrace, throwing missiles including paint and bricks at police, kicking in or attempting to kick in the doors of houses and smashing the windows of properties.

The court was also shown footage taken on a mobile phone from inside the ground floor flat of a property after Kane set fire to the kitchen.

Judge Peter Irvine KC said a family from Bulgaria had to be rescued from the upstairs flat including a pregnant woman suffering from smoke inhalation and a young child.

The court also viewed mobile phone footage taken by a family of eight adults and three children, including a three-year-old, who hid in the attic of a house in Clonavon Terrace for about four hours.

Kelvin Kane broke the building's front window and attempted to kick down an internal door before entering the property, the court was told.

Judge Irvine said the family, who were also from Bulgaria, were "clearly in a terrified state".

The court heard Kelvin Kane repeatedly targeted another property in Clonavon Terrace where a Filipino family lived, with the judge saying Kane seemed to find "particular satisfaction" attacking the home.

The judge said Kelvin Kane was the first person to throw missiles and objects at police.

"I also find that you organised and orchestrated this riot," the judge said.

"You are most certainly the leader and organiser and instigator of this particular series of disturbances that evening."

On several occasions in the CCTV footage Kelvin Kane was seen with his arms in the air, which Judge Irvine said appeared to be "an act of gratuitous celebration".

The footage showed Tracy Kane at several points filming the disorder, speaking to her son and apparently pointing things out to him.

Judge Irvine said she had done more than just assist Kelvin Kane, but had "instigated many of the events" and had been pointing out homes to him which were later attacked.

The judge said Tracy Kane "may not have physically participated in the riot itself" but had instigated and encouraged her son's "disgraceful violent activities".

He described her as a ringleader who "led and directed a group of rioters concerned over a lengthy and sustained period of time".

He said Tracy Kane had clearly taken "great pleasure" in the disorder and referenced her being heard on video footage saying that the riot was "even better than the Twelfth of July".

A defence barrister for Kelvin Kane said his client deeply regretted his involvement in the rioting and admitted what he did was "entirely unjustified and wrong".

He said Kelvin Kane had "a significant and longstanding history of drug misuse and associated homelessness" and that his initial involvement "was not solely controlled, driven or motivated by race".

A barrister representing Tracy Kane said his client had a difficult upbringing and suffered from problems with alcohol.

He said she felt genuine remorse and had made it clear to probation that her behaviour was "ridiculous".

Judge Irvine said in a report compiled by an educational psychologist, Kelvin Kane had expressed "deep regret" and accepted he would have to accept the consequences for his actions.

But he said Tracy Kane had "minimised her involvement" and had said she had become involved in the disorder out of a desire to protect her son.

The judge said this was "unacceptable and inconceivable" and that Tracy Kane was not trying to protect him, but encourage him.

"You are both a total and absolute disgrace to the decent law-abiding citizens of Ballymena," Judge Irvine said.

"You are violent individuals and you both glorified in the racial hatred that was displayed that evening and directed towards the minority ethnic community.

"Your behaviour must be utterly condemned by any sensible member of the public."

He added that their offences were aggravated by racially hostility.

Kelvin Kane was handed an eight-year sentence for the count of riot, with half to be served in prison and half on licence.

He will serve it concurrently with sentences for the other 16 counts.

Tracy Kane was handed a sentence of four years for the count of encouraging or assisting rioting, with half to be spent in prison and half on licence.

She was also sentenced to 40 months for a count of burglary with intent to cause unlawful damage, with half to be spent in prison and half on licence.

Both of her sentences will also run concurrently.

articles.title: Israeli bombardment has left Gaza a ‘toxic wasteland’ for decades to come, report says
articles.summary: The report said extensive use of explosive and incendiary weapons, airstrikes and fires has made the air, soil and water too dangerous to live in for decades to come.
articles.body: Israel’s military assault on Gaza has caused severe environmental contamination, with signs of toxic pollution found across the entire territory, according to a report published by Oxfam and the Conflict and Environment Observatory (CEOBS). The report, published Monday, said the extensive use of explosive and incendiary weapons, airstrikes and fires has made the air, soil and water too dangerous for inhabitants now and for decades to come. The scale and intensity of Israel’s bombardment have affected around 78% of Gaza’s landmass, with more than 99% of the territory experiencing potential contamination, the groups’ study found. “The destruction and contamination of Gaza will have fundamentally degraded the environmental conditions necessary for human safety and survival,” Oxfam International Executive Director Amitabh Behar said. “This would breach Israel’s legal obligations under international humanitarian and human rights law.” The report’s authors said that environmental destruction on such a large scale “may constitute, facilitate or provide powerful evidence of war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide.” Behar said Palestinians are being exposed to toxins through air, food, water and through direct contact with contaminated soils and debris — risks that will persist unless “recovery actions are prioritized.” Israel’s Foreign Ministry called the report “shameful and scandalous” and said Oxfam had “traded its credibility for campaigning.” “The scale of destruction in Gaza reflects the scale of the terror network Hamas built there, including a 500+ kilometer tunnel system and weapons depots, inside and beneath civilian areas,” the ministry said in a statement to CNN. The Board of Peace, created by the Trump administration and backed by a UN Security Council resolution, was supposed to oversee implementation of a ceasefire signed between Israel and Hamas more than a year ago, as well as reconstruction of the enclave. Amid a stalled ceasefire plan, the board is widely seen as having failed in that effort and as ineffective at pressuring Israel to meet its commitments. Israel has refused to allow in heavy equipment needed for large-scale cleanup and rubble removal efforts, saying Hamas could use it for military purposes. The Israeli military office in charge of coordinating aid into Gaza has said that reconstruction will begin only “after Hamas fully disarms.” Last December, Israel barred dozens of aid organizations, including Oxfam, from working in Gaza, alleging that they failed to comply with new registration restrictions. For the study published on Monday, Oxfam and CEOBS examined satellite imagery, remote sensing, scientific analysis and other open-source data. They concluded that contamination is widespread, with serious implications for civilian survival. But the report cautioned that restrictions on bringing testing equipment and technical expertise into Gaza “continue to prevent a full assessment of the scale and extent of contamination.” The United Nations Environment Program (UNEP) estimated last year that Israel’s military offensive has generated more than 61 million tons of debris — about as much as 15 Great Pyramids of Giza — which could contain potentially hazardous materials. Palestinians in Gaza face growing respiratory health risks from dust and pollution from destroyed buildings, as well as a high risk of drinking contaminated water, as water supply systems have been devastated. Around 85% of Gaza’s water infrastructure has been damaged or destroyed, according to the report, leaving people with roughly just 18 liters of water per person per day for all uses. The report warns that because Gaza’s health and monitoring systems have been destroyed, much of the harm caused by the toxic waste will go “undetected and unattributed for years.” Oxfam called on Israel to allow unrestricted access for aid and an environmental assessment. “Recovery and reconstruction of Gaza must be owned and led by Palestinians themselves,” the organization stated. “It must be rights-based, reparations-oriented, and rooted in accountability. International funding does not replace Israel’s obligation to make reparations for the harm caused by its unlawful acts.” Israel’s offensive in Gaza has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians since the Hamas-led attack on Israel on October 7, 2023, with estimates of thousands more missing under the rubble. An independent UN Commission of Inquiry found that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza and continues to do so after the US-brokered ceasefire. The Israeli government has forcefully rejected that assessment.

articles.title: Carney shares stage with Trump impersonator: ‘Fake news’
articles.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Saturday shared the stage with two impersonators –– one of himself and the other of President Trump –– at the annual Parliamentary Press Gallery dinner in Ottawa. Carney announced that he was “pressing the emergency comedy button” before comedian Mark McKinney appeared as Carney. Comedian Mark Critch, as Trump,…
articles.body:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Saturday shared the stage with two impersonators –– one of himself and the other of President Trump –– at the annual Parliamentary Press Gallery dinner in Ottawa.

Carney announced that he was “pressing the emergency comedy button” before comedian Mark McKinney appeared as Carney. Comedian Mark Critch, as Trump, emerged from the back of the room and walked to the podium, but not before mimicking the president’s dance seen at campaign events.

“Fake news. We’ve got two Carneys here. It’s a disaster. Isn’t this incredible? Two Carneys, he’s so popular, almost as popular as me. It’s like ‘Heated Rivalry’ if the hockey players were straight and all goalies,” Critch said, referring to the HBO Max series.

BestReviews is reader-supported and may earn an affiliate commission.

Critch added, in a nod to the real Trump’s references on the campaign trail last month to Sen. Jon Husted’s (R-Ohio) physique, that McKinney had “a great a–, doesn’t he? What a beautiful a–. He’s got such an incredible a–.”

He added that he’s “so popular, we just had a big blue wave,” talking about the sweeping Democratic victories in the 2026 midterm elections.

“So many people are leaving [Canadian opposition leader] Pierre Poilievre’s office that we’re going to have to build a wall, and Canada’s going to pay for it,” Critch continued. “They’re not sending their best. They’re really not. We’re going to have a deal though. We’re going to have a deal, aren’t we, Mark? We’re going to have an incredible deal.”

Audience members laughed and applauded as the fake Trump looked at both Carneys and said he would not call the prime minister “ the governor to his face because I’m a coward,” mocking the real Trump’s remarks about Canada becoming the 51st state .

“There’s only one thing standing in the way,” Critch said. “Me, because I’m crazy. But that’s OK.”

The event also lampooned other aspects of Canadian political life, with Poilievre mocking former Prime Minister Justin Trudeau, who is in a relationship with pop star Katy Perry, and comparing his time in office to a “faded pop princess.” This line drew criticism online.

Louise Arbour, Canada’s governor general, also poked fun at Carney for his international travel, saying that the difference between the prime minister and God is that “God is everywhere and Mark Carney is everywhere except in Ottawa where he’s supposed to be.”

Carney and Trump have been locked in a months-long tariff battle after trade negotiations fell apart in August.

Trump slapped 50 percent tariffs on many Canadian goods in August, even those covered under the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement, the trade agreement Trump himself signed in his first term. Canada hit back with retaliatory tariffs weeks later.

Trump and Carney separately said earlier this month that there had been progress in the talks, though Carney stressed to The New York Times’s Andrew Ross Sorkin that the relationship between the two countries cannot be repaired overnight.

articles.title: Spanish court removes last hurdle to Catalan leader’s return from exile
articles.summary: Spain’s Supreme Court shelved a criminal case against Catalan separatist and former regional leader Carles Puigdemont on Monday, thus removing the last legal hurdle for him to return to Spain following nearly a decade of self-imposed exile.
articles.body: Spain’s Supreme Court shelved a criminal case against Catalan separatist and former regional leader Carles Puigdemont on Monday, thus removing the last legal hurdle for him to return to Spain following nearly a decade of self-imposed exile. Puigdemont fled to Belgium in October 2017 after holding an independence referendum that the judiciary deemed illegal. The failed vote triggered a deep crisis between Madrid and the northeastern region, which has a distinct language and culture, as well as a significant secessionist movement that peaked in support that year. After the Constitutional Court ruled last month that the amnesty law for Catalan separatists also applied to embezzlement charges against Puigdemont and the Supreme Court lifted the warrant for his arrest, Monday’s ruling was the final step needed for Puigdemont’s return. Following the decision, Puigdemont posted on X a poem by Catalan author Jaume Pons Alorda containing foul language and directed at his “dearest enemies.” Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez’s government pushed through the amnesty under a 2023 agreement between his Socialist Party and two Catalan parties, including Puigdemont’s Junts, in exchange for their support to be re-elected as premier. The move unleashed intense social and political opposition from the government’s critics at the time. In a recent interview with newspaper El Mundo, Puigdemont said his party had taken advantage of what he described as Sanchez’s ambition in order to “defeat” Spain. He added he was in no hurry to return to Catalonia and had no plans to do so during the campaign ahead of the November 29 general election, but was considering coming back in December, on a date yet to be determined. Puigdemont will hold a press conference in Brussels on Wednesday, Junts said.

articles.title: Jury out in Huntingdon train attack attempted murder trial
articles.summary: Anthony Williams, 33, denies attempting to murder 10 passengers he stabbed on a London-bound train.
articles.body:
Jurors have been sent out to begin considering their verdicts in the trial of a knifeman accused of attempting to murder 10 people on a London-bound train.

Anthony Williams, 33, stabbed 10 passengers between Peterborough and Huntingdon, Cambridgeshire, on 1 November 2025.

He has also pleaded not guilty to the attempted murders of three people in Peterborough and a boy in London prior to the stabbings.

After summing up the evidence in the case at Cambridge Crown Court, the judge, Mr Justice Calver KC, sent the jury out to start its deliberations. It will resume on Tuesday.

"You are under no time pressure whatsoever," he told jurors.

Williams has admitted wounding with intent to cause really serious bodily harm in respect of 12 victims and attempting to do so to two others.

Ten of the victims were stabbed on an LNER service from Doncaster to London King's Cross.

Williams is also accused of trying to murder three people in Peterborough the day before, as well as attempting to murder a boy in the early hours of 1 November on a train in east London.

The judge said jurors needed to ask themselves if they were sure the defendant "intended to kill" each victim.

He said psychiatrists instructed by the prosecution and defence agreed Williams "was suffering from an acute psychosis as a result of his schizophrenia" at the time.

The judge referred to statements allegedly made by Williams to a psychiatrist, including that he believed "people sent by the devil" wanted to attack him.

Calver said the psychiatrist also recalled the defendant saying that "during the events it was all real, he was attacking real people with real knives" and "I just needed to protect myself, it was me or them".

The judge said a "person who is mentally ill, acting psychotically under a delusion, can still form an intent to kill".

Williams had made comments to people on the train including "do you want to die?" prosecutor Christopher Paxton KC said.

He said the defendant's alleged intention to kill "lay bare not just in his words... but in the slashes and stabs he inflicted not on the devil but on real people".

He noted Williams did not attack people on the platform before boarding the train.

"If there's a conspiracy by the devil, if it was Mr Williams saying, 'It's me or them', it's easier to kill people if they are trapped," Paxton said.

Gillian Jones KC said in her defence closing speech that Williams had been "in the clutches of an acute psychotic episode".

She gave examples of how Williams would start attacking a victim on the LNER train and then stop and walk away, and she said this was "consistent with a delusional belief he was under attack".

She said Williams "didn't intend to kill, he didn't intend to bring about death".

articles.body: Former Mossad chief David Barnea revealed Monday that Israeli intelligence played a key role in thwarting an ISIS-inspired terrorist plot targeting Taylor Swift's concerts in Vienna in 2024, an attack he said could have killed hundreds of young people. Speaking at the European Leadership Network ELNET conference in Jerusalem, Barnea disclosed that Austrian intelligence had initially identified the threat before turning to Israel's Mossad, which helped uncover the network behind the planned attack. "The initial threat warning came from our Austrian partners," Barnea said, according to the transcript of his speech. SPY LAW USED TO STOP TAYLOR SWIFT ATTACK TO LAPSE AS CONGRESS SKIPS TOWN, WORLD CUP NEARS Once Austrian authorities shared the information, the Mossad used its intelligence capabilities to analyze the threat, uncover the network and help bring about the suspects' arrests, Barnea said. The joint effort prevented "mass murder, up to hundreds of young European men and women," he said. The disclosure sheds new light on the international intelligence cooperation behind the foiled plot, which forced the cancellation of three sold-out shows during Swift's record-breaking "Eras Tour" in August 2024. More than 170,000 spectators were expected to attend the concerts, according to estimates from the Austrian news agency APA cited by The Times of Israel. Austrian authorities arrested the principal suspect, then 19, on Aug. 7, 2024, just one day before Swift was scheduled to perform at Vienna's Ernst Happel Stadium. Swift later described the cancellations as devastating and thanked authorities for preventing a tragedy. "Thanks to them, we were grieving concerts and not lives," she wrote on Instagram in August 2024. Austrian intelligence officials believed the suspect intended to attack crowds gathered outside the stadium, where an estimated 20,000 fans without tickets were expected to assemble. The investigation also involved American intelligence agencies. The Biden administration acknowledged in August 2024 that the United States had shared intelligence with Austrian authorities to help disrupt the threat. Then-White House national security spokesman John Kirby confirmed that American officials had provided information to their Austrian counterparts. The Vienna concert plot was not the only operation Barnea discussed. According to his remarks, he described Mossad's cooperation with European agencies against alleged Iranian-directed assassination plots and Hamas networks accused of preparing attacks on Jewish and Israeli targets. Barnea said Israeli intelligence helped expose an alleged Iranian network in Greece and North Macedonia and uncover cells in France and Germany. He also claimed that joint investigations with German, Austrian and Danish authorities revealed Hamas infrastructure and concealed weapons stockpiles in Vienna, Bulgaria and Poland. These were separate operations from the ISIS-linked Swift plot. A senior Israeli intelligence official told Fox News Digital at the time that active cells remained across Europe and warned that security agencies needed to remain vigilant. articles.title: Kaliningrad's $576 million lifeline, Russia plans railway ferries to bypass Europe's restrictions
articles.summary: Russia is moving to secure a vital supply lifeline to its Kaliningrad exclave through the Baltic Sea, as mounting tensions with European countries and
articles.body: Russia is moving to secure a vital supply lifeline to its Kaliningrad exclave through the Baltic Sea, as mounting tensions with European countries and restrictions on overland transit threaten its connectivity with mainland Russia.Moscow plans to spend $576 million on two new railway ferries to ensure essential goods and raw materials can reach the strategically important territory without relying on routes passing through EU member states.Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin on Monday announced that Moscow will spend 47 billion roubles ($576 million) to build two railway ferries for transporting goods to Kaliningrad.Most of the funding will come from Russia's National Wealth Fund. The two ferries are expected to enter service by 2030 and will operate between Ust-Luga, in Russia's Leningrad region, and Baltiysk in Kaliningrad, Reuters reported.The ferries will carry railway wagons loaded with essential goods, raw materials and other supplies across the Baltic Sea. The project is aimed at strengthening maritime transportation and ensuring uninterrupted deliveries to Kaliningrad, reducing Moscow's dependence on overland transit routes passing through European Union countries.Why is Russia building the ferries?Russia wants to reduce its dependence on overland supply routes passing through European countries, particularly Lithuania, and strengthen its alternative maritime corridor to Kaliningrad.The issue became more pressing in 2022, when Lithuania restricted the transit of several Russian goods, including construction materials, through its territory in compliance with European Union sanctions imposed after Moscow launched its invasion of Ukraine.Since then, Kaliningrad has become increasingly dependent on maritime transportation. According to Reuters, sea shipments now account for more than half of the region's supplies, compared with just 8% in 2021. Around 30 vessels, including four existing railway ferries, currently transport goods between Kaliningrad and Russian Baltic ports.Why is Kaliningrad so important for Russia?Kaliningrad is one of Russia's most strategically important territories because of its location on the Baltic Sea. Sandwiched between Poland and Lithuania, both Nato members, the exclave gives Moscow a significant military foothold in a region where the alliance has a strong presence.The region hosts the headquarters of Russia's Baltic Fleet and serves as a key military outpost, allowing Moscow to project power across the Baltic Sea and maintain a military presence close to Nato's eastern flank. It also hosts important military infrastructure, including missile systems and air defence installations.Historically, Kaliningrad was part of Germany and was known as Königsberg. It was captured by Soviet forces in April 1945 during the final stages of World War II.Under the post-war arrangements agreed at the Potsdam Conference in 1945, the territory was placed under Soviet control. In July 1946, the city was renamed Kaliningrad after Soviet leader Mikhail Kalinin.Following the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991, it became part of the Russian Federation, geographically separated from mainland Russia by independent states.Its geographical position is also its biggest vulnerability. Kaliningrad has no direct land connection with mainland Russia, making its supplies dependent on transit through neighbouring countries or maritime routes across the Baltic Sea.Any disruption to these routes could threaten the movement of essential goods and military supplies to the region.You use AI every day. articles.title: Russia warns Ukraine of ‘dangerous trend’ after Libya and Baltic attacks
articles.summary: Russia has reacted with fury to Ukraine’s continued campaign targeting its naval and merchant shipping.
articles.body:
Moscow has warned Ukraine that it will face “painful consequences” for its drone attacks on Russian vessels in Libya and the Baltic Sea.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters on Monday that Russia’s Ministry of Defence was handling the matter after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country’s forces had sunk two ships in the Libyan port of Benghazi.

Peskov said the ministry would release details if it deemed it appropriate, adding that Russia will continue its attacks on Ukraine in response.

“Our military personnel continue to carry out large-scale, comprehensive strikes on military infrastructure in Ukraine on a daily basis. This practice has very painful consequences for the Kyiv regime,” he said.

Peskov added that the Baltic attack was “escalating tensions” in the region while he said Moscow hoped the Baltic states would use their influence to press Kyiv to stop what he described as “terrorist practices”.

Zelenskyy said on Monday that Ukrainian forces sank the Russian corvette Merkury at a naval base in Benghazi on Sunday and struck a cargo ship he said Russia used to carry weapons.

Libya’s eastern-based government, a rival to the country’s internationally recognised western government in Tripoli, has lodged a complaint with the United Nations, saying the attacks violated Libyan sovereignty. It called for an international investigation into reports that Ukrainian military personnel were allegedly present in western Libya.

The attacks are part of Ukraine’s increased efforts to target naval assets and merchant ships linked to Moscow’s “shadow fleet”, which is used to help Russia evade Western sanctions.

A drone attack on Saturday set the Kaliningrad-bound Sparta II on fire in international waters in the Baltic Sea. Finland’s military said Ukraine likely carried out the attack.

Peskov also hit out at that attack, saying it marked a “very dangerous trend”.

The attack exposed Russia’s growing reliance on maritime transport.

On Monday, Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin said Moscow would spend 47 billion roubles ($576m) on two rail ferries to keep goods flowing to the exclave of Kaliningrad, which sits on the Baltic Sea coast between Lithuania and Poland, isolated from mainland Russia.

Lithuania restricted the transit of goods, including construction materials, from Russia to the exclave in line with European Union sanctions in 2022, leaving Kaliningrad heavily dependent on sea-borne supplies.

The ferries are expected to begin running between Ust-Luga and Baltiysk in 2030. Russia’s rainy-day fund will cover most of the cost, Mishustin said.

As so often, amid the rhetoric, Russian Security Council Deputy Chairman Dmitry Medvedev sought to up the ante, repeating his regular nuclear sabre rattling.

“Russia has the right, and in some circumstances the obligation, to use every means at its disposal to defend itself, potentially including nuclear weapons,” the former president wrote in an article published on Monday.

However, he conceded that while Ukraine and NATO countries continue to provoke Moscow, it has so far not seen a “direct necessity” to use nuclear weapons in its war in Ukraine.

articles.title: Miss Universe is embroiled in chaos. Again
articles.summary: One year after vote-rigging allegations, jury resignations and a contestant walkout enveloped the world’s biggest beauty pageant in scandal, Miss Universe is back. And surprise, surprise: It’s as chaotic as ever.
articles.body: One year after vote-rigging allegations, jury resignations and a contestant walkout enveloped the world’s biggest beauty pageant in scandal, Miss Universe is back. And surprise, surprise: It’s as chaotic as ever. Miss Universe’s 75th edition in Puerto Rico is still a day away, but this year’s controversies already include — but are, by no means, limited to — franchise disputes, a protest withdrawal, absent pageant co-owners, visa rejections and a shoddy unofficial runway event that saw contestants struggle to navigate a sandy beach in high heels. And there’s still Tuesday’s grand finale to come. The contestant list tells some of the story. Half of Southeast Asia is unrepresented this year due to a contractual dispute between organizers and businessman Nawat Itsaragrisil, who runs qualifying pageants in Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Singapore, Vietnam and his native Thailand. (It was, incidentally, Itsaragrisil who sparked last year’s walkout by criticizing eventual winner, Miss Mexico Fátima Bosch, in front of other contestants. He later apologized but denied calling her “dumb head.”) The disagreement appears to be exacerbated by the Miss Universe Organization’s messy ownership structure, which divides control between the seemingly-at-war MU East and MU West (more on that later), and a decentralized qualifying structure that licenses out national pageants to a who’s-who of local businesspeople in over 100 countries. Elsewhere, participants from Nepal and five African countries, including would-be debutants South Sudan and the Republic of Congo, have been forced to pull out due to US visa issues. The organizers of the Miss France pageant, meanwhile, withdrew their delegate in May in protest against last year’s turmoil — much of which centered on former judge Omar Harfouch’s claim that Bosch’s victory was pre-scripted, and that finalists were preselected in a “secret vote” by an unofficial “impromptu jury.” Miss Universe Organization has consistently denied the allegations. It also proceeded to form a selection committee that appointed a new Miss France, who has traveled to Puerto Rico for the final. What organizers haven’t done over the last year is rebuild confidence in the judging process. The criteria on which the women are ranked have always been broad and subjective, with no meaningful information ever published on how scores are assigned or weighted. Independent auditors like Ernst & Young, which once oversaw voting and handed hosts the results in sealed envelopes on stage, are now nowhere to be seen. Doubts about this year’s process have been compounded by organizers’ failure to reveal, at the time of publication, the identity of any judges for this year’s finale. By contrast, some of last year’s jury, including Harfouch, were announced weeks or even months in advance. “I would like contestants to know who will judge them, how the judges are selected, how scores are verified, and how conflicts of interest are handled,” Itsaragrisil told CNN via text message, adding that he hopes his six withdrawn Southeast Asian delegates can instead participate next year. Even die-hard fans are questioning Miss Universe’s future. Comments to a video posted on social media by pageant analyst Luis Portelles, who urged the organization to reveal this year’s judging panel ahead of the closed-door interview portion (“just tell us… release it!”) ranged from renewed allegations of a “cooked” result to calls for a boycott. As one fed-up commenter wrote, “Does it matter anymore?” It gets worse In another hangover from last year’s tumult, former Miss Jamaica Gabrielle Henry recently filed a lawsuit against the Miss Universe Organization. In it, she accuses organizers of “negligence” over a head injury she said she sustained after falling off stage during a 2025 preliminary event. Litigation is ongoing, and the Miss Universe Organization did not respond to CNN’s request for comment on the case. This may, however, be the least of organizers’ legal troubles. Simmering in the background of this already shambolic event are the scandal-plagued affairs of the pageant’s co-owners. Last year, Anne Jakrajutatip, founder of MU East’s owner JKN Global Group, was sentenced, in absentia, to two years in prison for fraud involving a 30-million-baht ($885,000) corporate bond investment, according to Thai media. The businesswoman and transgender rights activist failed to appear at a Bangkok court in December and now is considered at large. The Miss Universe Organization, which Jakrajutatip purchased for $20 million in 2022, announced last October that she had been replaced as CEO. And with JKN Global recently placed into receivership by a Thai bankruptcy court, her company’s part-ownership of Miss Universe has been thrown in doubt anyway. (Itsaragrisil, the Southeast Asian franchisee, claims he now effectively runs MU East, though his role is disputed by counterparts from the Western bloc.) On the pageant’s other side is Raúl Rocha Cantú, whose Legacy Holding Group owns MU West. The controversial Mexican businessman was at the center of last year’s tumult, accused by Harfouch of rigging the vote in Bosch’s favor because of apparent business ties to her father, an allegation Rocha Cantú vociferously denied. He then openly admitted on a livestream that the relative weakness of hotly tipped Miss Ivory Coast’s passport had counted against her, as she would need numerous visas to complete her globe-trotting duties as Miss Universe. In sum, the dumpster fire that is Miss Universe is burning more fiercely than ever. But is anyone even looking? In much of the West, increasingly not. Once a fixture on primetime network television, the English-language broadcast of the “Super Bowl” of pageants now only appears on streaming platforms in the US. The rapid decline in mainstream American viewership mirrors the fortunes of other pageants. Miss World is now on streaming service Fawesome; Miss USA and Miss America air on the specialist platforms Queen Beauty Network and PageantVision, respectively. It’s enough to make the era of Donald Trump, who owned Miss Universe from 1996 to the early 2000s, before co-owning it with NBC until 2015, look like veritable golden years. And commercially speaking, they may have been, according to Hilary Levey Friedman, a sociologist and author of the book “Here She Is: The Complicated Reign of the Beauty Pageant in America.” “A lot of their problems started after Donald Trump sold Miss Universe and Miss USA,” she said over the phone, adding that controversies over the now-US president’s ownership — including allegations he walked into dressing rooms while women were undressed or getting changed — only emerged after he sold the pageants and ran for office. A spokesperson from Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign denied the claims at the time. “There used to be, particularly with Miss Universe, way more stability in terms of who the owners were and who was running it,” Friedman said, adding: “There’s just been a lot more turnover in the past few years.” Spiraling into irrelevance Pageants’ commercial challenges are symptomatic of wider societal shifts. In the US, like many parts of the world, the events are increasingly seen as anachronisms that objectify women and promote singular beauty standards. Miss Universe’s recent attempts to modernize have done little to dispel this notion. The pageant’s decision to allow — gasp — mothers and married women to participate, starting in 2023, only served to remind everyone that, in this decade, mothers and married women hadn’t been able to take part. A rule banning over-28s was only lifted in 2024. Other rule changes have, arguably, helped dismantle prejudices. For one, Miss Universe has allowed trans women to participate since 2013 (although only after beauty queen Jenna Talackova was controversially disqualified from Miss Universe Canada). Progress on who can enter is not the same as who wins, however. “The same body types tend to win — we’ve seen an expansion of racial and ethnic diversity, sexuality, even some gender identity, but not so much different body types,” said Friedman, describing the “very real psychological issues” contestants may face due as a result. “Whenever you’re in a competition, you’re going to think, ‘Well, I just wasn’t good enough,’” she said. “And when this has to do with how you look, people will think, ‘Oh, I’m not thin enough, I’m not tall enough, I’m not ‘whatever’ enough.’ And that can be very difficult, because some of those are just immutable things about ourselves.” Miss Universe also perseveres with its hopelessly outdated swimsuit contest, launched in the early 1950s — an era it feels better suited to — as a marketing stunt for a swimwear manufacturer. More than seven decades on, the competition is still essentially a judged bikini parade (aside from a handful of contestants permitted to wear more modest burkinis on religious grounds.) While hardly constituting radical enlightenment, pageants like Miss World and Miss America have at least replaced their swimwear rounds with alternatives, including “athleisure.” Even then, however, the focus is often how your body looks not “what your body does,” Friedman said. But pageants’ ability to impact wider beauty standards is likely tempered by their declining social relevance, the author added. After all, compared to the events’ 1950s and ‘60s heyday, women and girls now contend with myriad other sources of unrealistic body ideals, whether reality TV or social media. Human cost It is possible to question the role of pageants in modern society while also enjoying the spectacle they bring. Take Miss Universe’s unashamedly bonkers national costume parade, which on Saturday saw contestants dress up in patriotic costumes resembling anything from a troll (Norway) to a golden frog (Costa Rica). Even then, though, the pageants couldn’t dodge controversy entirely, with Miss Israel audibly booed by audience members after unveiling the word “peace,” in three different languages, on her costume’s cape. On Tuesday, viewing parties will be held around the world, including in the parts of Africa, Asia and Latin America where pageantry enjoys continued, even growing, popularity. The show will be a source of pride for those who enjoy seeing — and cheering on — their country on the world stage. Think, especially, of pageant fans in Saint Martin and Uganda, which are making their Miss Universe debuts this year, or in Jordan and Tunisia, which are competing for the first time since 1960 and 1971, respectively. In many countries, pageants are everyday community events, while winning national competitions can present life-changing opportunities to young women. Even in the US, pageantry’s reputation differs by culture: Despite Miss Universe’s declining fortunes on American TV, the Spanish-language broadcast of 2025’s finale was viewed by 2.6 million people on Telemundo, up from 2.1 million the previous year. And while the chaos surrounding this year’s Miss Universe may make for car-crash viewing, there’s a human cost too. Take Miss Singapore, Vion Tan, who wrote on Instagram that her forced withdrawal had “hit me harder than I can put into words.” “This journey was never just about a crown or a competition,” she added. “It was about the opportunity to carry Singapore’s name onto an international stage, to share our culture, our stories and the spirit of a small nation with big dreams.”

articles.title: MICHAEL RUIZ: 911 call reveals chase before disputed 'stand your ground' shooting, ‘He's trying to run’
articles.summary: An eight-minute 911 call captured the Highway 9 road rage clash that left Scott Spivey dead, and two South Carolina men now face murder charges.
articles.body: An eight-minute recorded 911 call captured the harrowing road rage clash that ended in the death of a North Carolina man after an alleged shootout with a South Carolina bar owner and his friend, who were charged with murder more than three years later. "I've got a guy pointing a gun at me driving, we're armed as well," a man, later identified as driver Charles "Weldon" Boyd, tells the dispatcher. "He keeps throwing the gun at our faces, acting like he's about to shoot us. If he keeps this up, I'm gonna shoot him. I'm on Highway 9. He's trying to run from me now." They were heading north on Highway 9 from North Myrtle Beach. 'STAND YOUR GROUND' CLAIM FALTERS IN ROAD RAGE KILLING AS MEN CHARGED WITH MURDER, EX-COPS FACE ACCUSATIONS "We're headed toward Loris," Boyd says. "I'm gonna stay with him the whole way. Y'all need to get this guy off the road. He's aiming guns at people. He racked it." By the end of the altercation, 33-year-old insurance adjuster Scott Spivey was dead on Camp Swamp Road, 9 miles from where he first encountered Boyd, 35, and Kenneth "Bradley" Williams, 37. LISTEN TO THE CALL: At one point, Boyd told the dispatcher Spivey was still brandishing the firearm and swerving at him on the road. "I need a trooper, fast," he said. SECRET TAPES SINK SHOOTER'S DEFENSE IN SCOTT SPIVEY ROAD RAGE KILLING He later tells the dispatcher they are pulling off the highway onto Camp Swamp Road. He says the other driver emerged armed. A voice believed to be Williams' can be heard telling Boyd to back up before gunfire erupts. "Weldon, back up!" the voice shouts. "I can't," Boyd replies. "I can't put it in gear!" In about 12 seconds, more than two dozen shots can be heard. "Goddamn it Weldon," the voice says after the shooting stops. "Why couldn't we f---ing leave him alone?" Boyd tells the dispatcher the other driver shot first and begs for police to arrive. Boyd and Williams were indicted on murder charges last week, more than a year after Spivey's sister and The Wall Street Journal made other recordings recovered from Boyd's phone public. They had originally invoked South Carolina's "stand your ground" law and said that Spivey pulled a gun on them first, without provocation, and ran them off the road as they were towing a trailer laden with furniture, according to court documents in a civil wrongful death case. Two former Horry County police officials, onetime deputy chief Brandon Strickland, 43, and 49-year-old Paul Damon Vescovi, were also charged for allegedly steering the investigation in Boyd's favor. All but Williams had posted bail as of Monday morning, according to the county sheriff's website. According to O'Bryan Martin, Williams' attorney, 911 dispatchers had received other calls about Spivey's erratic driving before his initial encounter with Boyd and Williams. "He was, for lack of better words, out of control, driving down that highway, committing multiple felonies, mind you, along the way," Martin told Fox News Digital. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB He said the autopsy report, surveillance footage, cellphone data, witness interviews and other evidence back up that position. "All things that can be corroborated and seen — I believe that they are uncontroverted," Martin told Fox News Digital. "Other people begin to make 911 calls about an individual who we now know to be Scott Spivey waving the pistol, driving erratically and dangerously down the highway, calling it road rage, calling it erratic, calling dangerous." GOT A TIP? In the civil case, the defense has also pointed to autopsy findings showing Spivey had a 0.13 blood alcohol content. articles.title: Virginia, Oregon sue Musk’s SpaceX over Grok AI’s creation of child sexual abuse images
articles.summary: Virginia and Oregon sued Elon Musk’s SpaceX Super Intelligence Corp on Monday, alleging the company profited from a feature in its AI model Grok that produces child sexual abuse material and other nonconsensual sexual images from photographs while failing to put safeguards in place to stop it.
articles.body: Virginia and Oregon sued Elon Musk’s SpaceX Super Intelligence Corp on Monday, alleging the company profited from a feature in its AI model Grok that produces child sexual abuse material and other nonconsensual sexual images from photographs while failing to put safeguards in place to stop it. Several state attorneys general had announced investigations into Grok over similar claims in recent months, but Virginia and Oregon were the first states to sue. The lawsuits filed in state courts accuse SpaceX of misleading consumers about Grok’s safety and failing to put adequate safeguards in place while promoting its “spicy mode.” That mode allows users to take an existing photograph of a person and generate a sexual or nude image or video, according to the lawsuits. Virginia and Oregon accused SpaceX of violating their respective consumer protection laws. They are seeking damages, penalties and court orders forcing the company to stop violating state law. SpaceX did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Grok is available to users of X, the social media platform that is a subsidiary of SpaceX. In a statement posted on X on Monday that didn’t directly address the lawsuits, the platform’s safety team said it had taken action to block prompts that could generate this type of imagery and worked with law enforcement to pursue people who use the platform to make it. “The people who tried to use Grok Imagine to generate this material did so by deliberately violating our Terms of Service and working aggressively to circumvent our safeguards,” the company posted. Virginia’s lawsuit cites data from a study by the Center for Countering Digital Hate, which estimated that between December 2025 and January 2026, Grok generated and posted on X millions of sexualized images, including more than 20,000 depicting children. Investigators from the attorney general’s office in Virginia found that Grok’s image moderation was inconsistent, and that the bot would advise users on how to circumvent the moderation measures by avoiding words that triggered it, according to the lawsuit. Beginning in January, Grok told users that its image generation features were only for paying subscribers, which did not stop the images’ creation but allowed the company to profit from them, the lawsuit said. States across the US have filed a growing number of lawsuits against social media and AI companies over harm they say the companies have caused to their residents. In an interview with Reuters ahead of Monday’s filings, Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones said state attorneys general are acting as a regulatory force in the tech industry, including on artificial intelligence, which has faced relatively little federal regulation so far. “In the absence of federal action, AGs have stepped into the breach,” Jones said. SpaceX is facing more than a dozen lawsuits brought by individuals who say nonconsensual sexual images of them as minors or adults were generated by Grok. In the UK, lawmaker Jess Asato is suing SpaceX ‌after Grok users generated sexualized images of her. The company has denied the claims, arguing that obviously fictitious, AI-generated content cannot breach someone’s right to privacy. In mid-January, xAI said it restricted image editing in Grok and blocked users from generating images of people in revealing clothing “where it’s illegal.” SpaceX acquired xAI in February and rebranded its AI division from xAI to SpaceX Super Intelligence in October. Reuters found in February that, even after new curbs, Grok continued to generate sexualized images of people even when users explicitly warned ⁠that the ​subjects did not consent. The company did not address detailed questions ​from Reuters about Grok’s generation of sexualized material. SpaceX is suing at least two people in the US alleging they misused Grok to create child sexual abuse material.

articles.summary: Prosecutors say Natalie Greene paid a body modification artist $500 to slash her face and neck before staging an anti-Trump attack in New Jersey.
articles.body: A federal grand jury has indicted a former aide to Rep. Jeff Van Drew, R-N.J., and her alleged co-conspirator over a staged political attack in which prosecutors say she paid $500 to have her own face and neck slashed and had anti-Trump slurs written on her body before calling 911. The indictment, filed in U.S. District Court in New Jersey, charges Natalie Greene of Ocean City with conspiracy, conveying false information and hoaxes, and making false statements to the FBI. The indictment also publicly names Greene's alleged co-conspirator as Anamaria Moe of Ventnor, who has been charged with conspiracy and hoax counts. FORMER AIDE TO HOUSE REP ACCUSED OF FAKING POLITICAL ATTACK Prosecutors allege the pair fabricated a July 23, 2025, ambush at the Egg Harbor Township Nature Reserve in New Jersey, claiming three armed men attacked them over Greene's work for Van Drew — identified in the charging document only as "Federal Official 1." Greene is accused of driving to the Pennsylvania studio of a body modification artist — identified in the indictment only as "Individual 1" — that day, when she "presented personal identification, submitted a legal waiver form for the scarification procedure, and hired [the person] to perform the scarification procedure in exchange for $500." DEM HOUSE HOPEFUL ALLEGES SHE WAS BRUTALLY ATTACKED DURING 2 AM CAMPAIGN ERRAND According to the indictment, Greene first messaged the Pennsylvania scarification artist on June 3, 2025, sending a photo showing a design with slashes across the neck, face and arm area before scheduling the procedure. Two days before the alleged attack, someone used Moe's cellphone to search online for "zip ties near me," prosecutors said. COP FIRED OVER FAKE FACEBOOK PAGE TARGETING MOM "On or about the evening of July 23, 2025, before GREENE and MOE went to the Nature Reserve, a member of the conspiracy wrote 'Trump Whore' on GREENE's stomach in black ink and '[Federal Official 1] is Racist' on her back," the indictment states. SEND US A TIP "GREENE was crying and yelling statements, including 'he has a gun,'" prosecutors wrote in the charging document, noting that officers recovered matching zip ties inside Greene's Maserati that same night. FBI HUNTS MOST WANTED NEIGHBOR NEXT DOOR WHO ALLEGEDLY FAKED CANCER, SCAMMED LOVED ONES FOR LUXURY GETAWAYS GOT A TIP? After being treated at a hospital, Greene doubled down on the story during a July 25 interview with an FBI special agent and local detectives, claiming two men pulled her shirt over her head, struck her in the head, cut into her body and pressed an object against her stomach that she believed was a gun. articles.title: Iranian authorities flog singer who performed without hijab, lawyers say
articles.summary: Parastoo Ahmadi, three musicians and a producer were reportedly given 74 lashes in Qom.
articles.body:
A prominent singer who performed without the mandatory hijab and four members of her band and production team have been flogged by Iranian authorities, lawyers say.

Parastoo Ahmadi, three musicians and a producer were each given 74 lashes in the city of Qom, a member of their defence team told the BBC.

Ahmadi, 29, wore a sleeveless dress during a concert that was livestreamed in December 2024. Iran's laws ban public performances by women and require them to wear headscarves and modest clothing.

This June, a criminal court in Qom convicted Ahmadi and eight others of "offending public decency" through the publication of "obscene and indecent material", which they had denied.

In addition to being sentenced to 74 lashes, they were banned from audiovisual activities and from leaving the country for two years.

At the end of September, an appeals court in Qom rejected the defendants' appeal and confirmed the sentence, her lawyers said.

There was widespread condemnation of the sentences from other Iranian artists and human rights activists, who warned that flogging constituted cruel, inhuman and degrading punishment, and violated the international prohibition on torture.

On Monday, one of the defendants' lawyers told the BBC that Ahmadi and four of her male co-defendants had been flogged at the third branch of the Criminal Sentence Enforcement Office in Qom.

"We did everything in our power to have the verdict overturned, or at least to secure a reduction in the sentence or a suspension, but it didn't work out," he said.

"The other lawyers and I even tried to get the enforcement of the sentence postponed, but the enforcement branch insisted on carrying it out immediately."

Pro-reform daily Etemad cited another defence lawyer, Mostafa Nili, as identifying the four men flogged alongside Ahmadi as Soheil Faghih-Nasiri, Amin Taheri, Amirali Pirnia and Mohsen Lashkari.

"Parastoo Ahmadi's flogging for singing and dressing as she chooses is a flagrant violation of her fundamental rights and a chilling demonstration of the Iranian authorities' determination to suppress women's freedoms and to violently punish anyone who dares to challenge their discriminatory laws and policies," said Bahar Ghandehari, director of advocacy at the US-based Center for Human Rights in Iran (CHRI).

Under Iranian law, which is based on the country's interpretation of Sharia, women and girls above the age of puberty must cover their hair with a hijab and wear long, loose-fitting clothing to disguise their figures.

In 2022, protests swept across the Islamic Republic following the death in custody of Mahsa Amini, a 22-year-old Kurdish woman who was detained by morality police in Tehran in September that year for allegedly wearing her hijab "improperly".

Women burnt their headscarves or waved them in the air at the nationwide demonstrations against the clerical establishment, during which hundreds of people were killed in a crackdown by security forces.

Since then, many women and girls have stopped covering their hair in public altogether in open defiance of the dress code. Authorities have responded with periodic waves of arrests, warnings, business closures and other measures.

In January this year, thousands of people were killed and tens of thousands were arrested when security forces crushed another wave of mass anti-establishment protests, this time sparked by the country's economic crisis.

Since the start of Iran's war with the US and Israel in late February, authorities have intensified their use of the death penalty against protesters.

According to the Norway-based group Iran Human Rights, at least 39 men convicted over January's protests and two convicted over the 2022 unrest have been executed, along with 16 people allegedly affiliated with banned opposition groups and 17 others convicted of espionage or collaborating with foreign states.

Another 121 protesters detained in January, including six women and five juvenile offenders, have been sentenced to death and are at imminent risk of execution, it says.

articles.title: Slain firefighter's mother pleads with Trump to intervene after Newsom stops killer's death sentence
articles.summary: Mother of firefighter Daniel Najera hopes President Trump can intervene in Gov. Gavin Newsom's commutation of arsonist Raymond Lee Oyler's death sentence.
articles.body: The mother of a 20-year-old firefighter killed in a deliberately set California wildfire is pleading for justice following Gov. Gavin Newsom's move to commute hundreds of death sentences, including that of the man convicted of murdering her son. "I'm hoping that President Trump will reverse this commutation," Gloria Najera-Ayala told "Fox & Friends" ahead of a planned meeting with the president on Monday. "It's very important for us to see it happen, because we sat in the courtroom for many, many months. And 12 jurors, there was a judge, there were over 100 witnesses that testified against Raymond Lee Oyler. Does that mean nothing?" NEWSOM'S BID TO EMPTY CALIFORNIA'S DEATH ROW COLLIDES WITH VOTERS' REPEATED REJECTION OF ABOLITION Najera-Ayala's son, Daniel Najera, was among five firefighters killed in the 2006 Esperanza Fire set by convicted serial arsonist Raymond Lee Oyler, who was later sentenced to death for his crimes. Oyler's death sentence is now among hundreds that Newsom seeks to commute to life imprisonment without the possibility of parole, a far-reaching move that has drawn opposition from prosecutors and victims' families. "Justice was taken away without a word to any of the victims' families," Najera-Ayala said. "None of us were informed... That was like the rug being pulled right out of us," she added. MICHAEL RUIZ: HALF OF CALIFORNIA'S DAS SUE NEWSOM OVER DEATH ROW CLEMENCY President Trump is expected to appear alongside Attorney General Todd Blanche and FBI Director Kash Patel at the Department of Justice (DOJ) on Monday afternoon to condemn the Democratic governor's proposed commutations, the White House confirmed to Fox News Digital. Families of murder victims, including Najera-Ayala, are expected to attend the event, where their stories will be highlighted. Newsom's commutation push still needs California Supreme Court approval for inmates with multiple felony convictions, including Oyler. "I hope he sees our pain. I hope that he listens to us and understands what we're going through, what we've gone through," Najera-Ayala said. "Nobody can take that grief away from us. We're living a sentence of grief for the rest of our lives." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP In a letter following the decision, Newsom wrote: "California voters have voted to keep the death penalty on the books, and I respect that... But the constitution also gave every governor clemency authority, and that power exists for moments when law as applied cannot be squared with justice. For me, this is that moment." "Fox & Friends" reached out to Newsom's office for comment but did not receive an immediate response. Fox News Digital's Jasmine Baehr contributed to this report.

articles.title: A Pennsylvania mother left her real estate to one son and the rest of her estate to a church, while a $218,891 state care claim was settled for about $40,000; a daughter's bid to remove the executor has failed
articles.summary: A Pennsylvania appeals court has rejected a woman's attempt to remove her brother as the executor of their late mother's estate, ruling that she lacked
articles.body: A Pennsylvania appeals court has rejected a woman's attempt to remove her brother as the executor of their late mother's estate, ruling that she lacked legal standing to pursue the case over a disputed $218,891 healthcare debt.The Pennsylvania Superior Court upheld a lower court's decision dismissing Ann Elizabeth Miller's petition against her brother, Andrew Chonko, who was appointed executor of their mother Charlotte Jane Chonko's estate. The ruling, filed on November 19, 2026, said Miller's concerns about potentially becoming responsible for the outstanding debt were speculative and did not give her a sufficient legal interest to challenge the estate's administration.According to the court records, the Pennsylvania Department of Human Services (DHS) had initially informed the estate in March 2024 that it owed $218,891.16 for their mother's care. However, the department later agreed to accept $40,037.19, the amount remaining in the estate, to settle its claim.Why did the woman seek her brother's removal as executor?Miller filed a petition in May 2025 seeking her brother's removal, accusing him of breaching his fiduciary responsibilities. She alleged that he had sold their mother's properties below market value, engaged in self-dealing and withheld information and personal belongings belonging to other family members.She also argued that the alleged handling of the estate could expose her and her siblings to liability for the outstanding healthcare debt under Pennsylvania's Filial Support Law, which places certain financial responsibilities on children to support indigent parents.The estate denied the allegations and argued that Miller had no standing to pursue the case because she was not a beneficiary under their mother's will.The will, signed in June 2021, named Andrew Chonko as executor, left him real estate and directed that the remaining estate go to Holy Trinity Lutheran Church in Berlin, Pennsylvania.The estate also pointed out that DHS had explicitly stated that its claim was against the estate and not the family members personally.What did the court say about the $218,000 debt?The appeals court said DHS had agreed to accept $40,037.19 from the estate in satisfaction of its claim. It noted that Miller's argument depended on several possible developments, including the discovery of additional hidden assets, DHS seeking further recovery and then attempting to collect money from the deceased woman's children.The court described this chain of possibilities as too speculative to establish a direct and immediate financial interest.It also referred to Pennsylvania's estate recovery law, which allows DHS to recover certain medical assistance payments from the probate estates of people aged 55 or older. The law also provides for liability in certain circumstances involving transfers of property before the department's claim is satisfied.The court, however, found that these provisions did not establish Miller's claimed personal financial risk in the circumstances of the case.Court rejects challenge over mother's willMiller had also questioned whether her mother was mentally capable of signing the will, citing dementia-related illnesses, prescribed medication and her own observations.However, the court noted that the will had been admitted to probate on March 12, 2024, while Miller raised the challenge on May 30, 2025, beyond the one-year statutory deadline for contesting probate.The appeals court said there was no claim that the executor had committed fraud on the Register of Wills or that the document presented as the will was fraudulent, circumstances that could potentially justify an exception to the deadline.It also rejected Miller's argument that the lower court had wrongly ended discovery before the extended deadline. The judges said the additional evidence she hoped to gather about her mother's mental capacity or possible undue influence would not change the fact that her challenge to the will was filed too late.The Pennsylvania Superior Court consequently affirmed the lower court's order dismissing her petition.You use AI every day.
